newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TITLE PRESSURE ON BAYERN AGAINST STUTTGART.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TITLE PRESSURE ON BAYERN AGAINST STUTTGART.

text.p: Three times in the last six years Bayern Munich have stumbled when in sight of the championship.
That unhappy record is bound to prey on their minds when they host VfB Stuttgart in their penultimate Bundesliga match on Saturday with just a one point lead over second placed Bayer Leverkusen.
Bayern have been German champions 13 times, and dominated the 1980s by winning the title six times.

But this decade they have so far won the Bundesliga only twice, in 1990 and 1994. In three other years, 1991, 1993 and 1996, they looked headed for the title but blew their chances with late season slumps.
As a result, the club has changed coaches almost every season since 1990.

"In Bayern, nerves are frazzled because there are several things in that team which don't go together," said Rudi Voeller, the former World Cup striker and now Bayer Leverkusen's sporting director, in an interview with Sport Bild on Wednesday.

Bayern president Franz Beckenbauer, who stepped in himself to coach late last year in a futile bid to win the championship, added to the pressure after Bayern's poor performance against Freiburg two weeks ago.
"On this form we have zero chance of winning the championship," Beckenbauer said after the 0-0 draw against Freiburg that enabled Leverkusen to move to within one point.

Those weren't exactly encouraging words from Beckenbauer, whose frustration followed the team's second consecutive draw against lesser opponents. Bayern drew 3-3 the week before against local rivals 1860 Munich.

The mood was dark before the team rallied for a 3-0 win against Rostock last week, but Leverkusen stayed in hot pursuit with a 3-0 victory over Hamburg, their third win in a row and 10th consectutive home triumph.
"We were feeling a lot of pressure," said Bayern striker Juergen Klinsmann of the win over Rostock. "The first goal there was a huge release. We had some real team spirit after that."

Beckenbauer said the Munich players know they have to win against Stuttgart and at Borussia Moenchengladbach, in eighth place and always difficult to defeat at home, in the final game of the season to win the championship.

"Perhaps there is more foolishness when we play at home against so-called 'easy' opponents," Beckenbauer said. "But that is all in the past now. The team knows that it has to win the last two games for the title."
Leverkusen, who just avoided relegation last season, have an easier schedule with matches at 10th-placed Cologne on Saturday and at home against fifth-placed Bochum in their final match.
Stuttgart are the highest-scoring side in the Bundesliga with 72 goals, 10 more than Bayern. They led the league for several weeks in the first half before slipping after the winter break.
"We don't have anything more to lose and we very much want to win now in Munich," said Stuttgart's Giovane Elber.
The striker, who will move to Bayern next year, is one of several Stuttgart players high in the Bundesliga scoring charts.
The Brazilian has scored 17 this season while his strike partner Fredi Bobic has 18 and midfielder Krassimir Balakov 13.
Stuttgart have won the Bundesliga four times, the last time in 1992 under Christoph Daum, now Leverkusen's trainer. A win for them on Saturday would do their old coach a big favour.
